analysis.procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): read operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. Define DP[i][j] as the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing the subexpression a[i] op[i] ... op[j-1] a[j]. Base case DP[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L from 2 to n, for each i with j=i+L-1, initialize DP[i][j]=empty set. For each split k from i to j-1, combine every x in DP[i][k] with every y in DP[k+1][j] using op[k]: if '+', add x+y; if '-', add x-y; if '*', add x*y. Insert results into DP[i][j]. Return the size of DP[0][n-1]. Use exact integer arithmetic and sets for deduplication.

response.applicability: Valid for inputs matching the schema: 1 to 8 integer operands in [-10,20] and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from +, -, *. Booleans are rejected as operands. Returns a nonempty numeric string. Does not handle other operators, reordering, or partial parenthesizations. Complexity is bounded by the small operand limit; intermediate value sets could in principle grow, but with at most 8 operands and small operands the computation is feasible.
response.description: Dynamic programming over contiguous operand intervals. For each interval [i,j], dp[i][j] is the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing operands i..j with the operators between them. Base intervals are single operands. For longer intervals, every split point k combines each value from the left interval with each value from the right interval using the operator at position k, inserting results into a set to deduplicate. The answer is the cardinality of the full-interval set. Exact integer arithmetic is used. Uncertainty: this assumes the intended interpretation is all full binary parenthesizations preserving left-to-right order, which matches the stated problems.
